messages:
Leah Morgan: FYI customer support flagged several tenants that missed the 30-day deprecation window because their billing contact was inactive. They expect a one-off extension rather than immediate enforcement. Can we propose an "auto-extension" heuristic instead of manual credits?

Samir Patel: I like automating it, but we need rules to avoid abuse. Suggest criteria: 1) tenant had >= 10% of traffic still routed to v1 in the last 7 days (meaning they're actively using the deprecated path), 2) billing contact hasn't accepted notices but tenant has active usage, 3) not previously auto-extended in last 180 days. If all true, extend grace by +14 days automatically and notify owners.

Tess Yu: Also add safety checks: do not extend if tenant has >X outstanding quota violations or if they are on a security-restricted plan. We should check tenant.policy: if they explicitly set `deprec_policy: DENY` then don't auto-extend.

Ben Rao: Implementation notes: router emits deprecation_hit events with tenant_id, route, last_active_ts. We'll run a nightly job that looks for eligible tenants and writes an extension_record to billing_db. Pseudo SQL:
```sql
INSERT INTO deprec_extensions (tenant, reason, expires_at)
SELECT t.id, 'auto-extend', now() + interval '14 days'
FROM tenants t
JOIN usage_last7 u ON u.tenant = t.id
LEFT JOIN deprec_extensions e ON e.tenant = t.id AND e.expires_at > now()
WHERE u.v1_pct >= 0.10
  AND t.deprec_policy != 'DENY'
  AND e.tenant IS NULL;
```
We must audit every auto-extension.

Leah Morgan: Console UX: show a small green pill on tenant billing page: "Deprecation grace extended (14d) — auto" with link to audit entry and an option to request manual override. Also send email to billing contact and post in tenant activity log.

Samir Patel: Telemetry: track `auto_extension_count`, `auto_extension_reversal_count` (when ops manually revokes), and delta in active_v1_pct during extension. If auto-extension correlates with increased v1 usage length, flag for product review.

Tess Yu: Edge-case: race with quota enforcement. If quota enforcer runs after we auto-extend but before we update quota windows, customers may still be throttled. Order of operations matters: write extension record first, then emit a cache inval to quota service. We'll add a short TTL cache and a sync signal.

Ben Rao: Billing/finance: auto-extension is a policy decision. Finance prefers issuing credits over changing enforcement rules that affect revenue recognition. Propose: auto-extension only postpones enforcement (no invoice change) and support can grant credits manually case-by-case. I'll loop in finance for approval.

opsbot: Ticket PLAT-4120 created: auto-extension nightly job + console pill + audit logging. Canaries: staging tenants only.

Leah Morgan: OK owners: Samir (eligibility + telemetry), Ben (quota ordering + finance), Tess (console mock + policy checks). We'll hold on full rollout until finance signs off. I'll draft FAQ for customers explaining auto-extension criteria and manual credit channels.

Ben Rao: One more safety: add `X-Deprecation-Grace` header on responses when a request benefited from an auto-extension so SDKs/clients can surface it. Header format: `X-Deprecation-Grace: auto;expires=2026-05-12T15:00:00Z`

Tess Yu: Nice. That will help customer support correlate logs. Thanks all — let's aim for staging deploy next week.
